newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels snatch U.S. geologist in southern Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Rebels snatch U.S. geologist in southern Colombia.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas have kidnapped a U.S. geologist working on a gold mining project in the south of Colombia, police said on Tuesday.

Frank Steek, 25, was snatched on March 7, together with a Colombia co-worker, Hermes Torres, after they were held up at a roadblock set up by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels in Narino province.

Provincial police chief Col. Fortunato Guanarita said Steek, whose home town was not known, had been working close to the town of Magui on the Pacific coast when he was seized. He said he had no knowledge of any ransom demand.

In early February, suspected Marxist rebels abducted Houston oilman Gerald Schaffer in Venezuela and are believed to have brought him across the border into Colombia. His current whereabouts are not known.
Another U.S. geologist Frank Pescatori, of Alabama-based mining company Geomet, was kidnapped by unidentified gunmen in December and was found shot to death in northern Colombia Feb. 25.
